Subject: Clarify delivery expectations for hybrid endpoint POC

Hi Vanessa —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. One follow-up from our engineering and procurement teams: we need the POC to make explicit commitments around streaming vs non-streaming behavior. Specifically:

- Time-to-first-token (TTFT) expectation for streaming endpoints under realistic burst load (we saw spikes to ~600 concurrent sessions).
- Sustained token/sec expectations for non-streaming endpoints (bulk re-ranking jobs) and how that maps to reserved capacity.
- What happens if TTFT slips for more than N% of requests — do you provide credits, automatic fallback, or mitigations?

I've attached a short spreadsheet with our expected traffic patterns and a sample telemetry export. Can you confirm if Redwood can meet: TTFT <= 120ms (p50) for streaming, and sustained 2k tokens/sec per reserved pod for non-streaming? If not, what carveouts or mitigations would you propose?

We'd like to capture these in the statement of work for the POC.

Thanks,
Elena Morales
Head of Integrations, ClearSky Health

Subject: Re: Clarify delivery expectations for hybrid endpoint POC

Elena —

Appreciate the detailed traffic patterns and the telemetry export. Short answers up front: we can aim for a p50 TTFT of <=120ms in many typical streaming configs, but hitting that under sustained multi-tenant burst (600 concurrent) without pre-warmed capacity will require a Dedicated capacity reservation or hybrid prewarming. For non-streaming batch work, 2k tokens/sec per reserved pod is achievable with a 16k context model on our dedicated SKU, but it depends on request size and quantization.

Key tradeoffs and mitigations we recommend:
- Dedicated pre-warmed pool for your peak windows (recommended) — guarantees delivery profile and reduces cold-start TTFT variance.
- Routing policy: route latency-sensitive sessions to pre-warmed pool, fallback to best-effort shared pool with degraded TTFT and token pacing.
- Observability: we will surface a per-route TTFT histogram and a per-pod token/sec metric; suggest we add a synthetic probe that exercises a short prompt every 30s.
- Credits: we typically offer SLA credits for sustained misses beyond the committed window. For the POC we can offer a conditional credit schedule tied to p99 TTFT breaches over a rolling 24-hour window.

I'll loop in engineering to call out the exact numbers and a proposed clause. Attaching a short delivery-profile sketch.

Next steps: can we schedule a 30-min tech sync with your TechOps tomorrow to validate the telemetry? I can bring Vivek (inference lead) and Lauren (sales lead on legal terms).

—Vanessa
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Hi Elena / ClearSky procurement team —

Quick note on commercial mechanics. For the POC we can include the following in the SOW:

- Commitment band: p50 TTFT <= 120ms for streaming routes when routed to Dedicated pre-warmed pool; fallback to shared pool documented as "best-effort" with expected p50 in 200-350ms under heavy burst.
- Token throughput: reserved pod SKU rated at ~2k tokens/sec for average token size; we'll include a calibration test in the POC to lock the effective token/sec guarantee and price tier.
- Credits & remediation: for sustained p99 TTFT violations (>1% of requests in 24h), 10% credit of daily invoice; escalations route to Redwood Ops on a 2-hour remediation SLA.

If procurement prefers a stricter credit schedule (e.g., 25% for major p99 breaches), we can escalate to legal but that will require additional margin.

Aditya
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai

Date: Tue, 12 Sep 2028 13:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify delivery expectations for hybrid endpoint POC

Elena —

Tech notes from the inference side (quick and practical):

- TTFT definition: we measure TTFT as time from request ingress to first token bytes on the wire at the agent boundary. Network latency at your edge isn't included; we'll provide an instrumented client to measure end-to-end in your env.
- Cold start causes: model loading, KV cache miss, and kernel dispatch. For streaming, KV cache warmup matters — we propose a small warmup traffic injection before peak windows.
- Graceful degradation: when capacity is constrained we support progressive delivery (first N tokens allowed, then throttle) and an automatic model-variant fallback to a smaller quantized model that preserves semantics with slightly higher latency.
- Token/sec accounting: we bill based on emitted tokens; for SLOs we tie the guarantee to the reserved pool's observed token emission rate averaged over 5-min windows. Spiky bursts are smoothed with request queueing; very large spikes may be subject to rate-limiting per route (we'll publish limits in config).

I'll prepare a short tech appendix that defines the measurement points, synthetic probe config, and fallback behavior. That should make the SOW language precise.

—Vivek
Head of Inference Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai

Date: Wed, 13 Sep 2028 10:09:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify delivery expectations for hybrid endpoint POC

Elena / procurement —

Following internal review, suggested SOW language for your counsel to review (high level):

1) Service commitments: Redwood will maintain for the POC a per-route p50 TTFT <= 120ms and per-reserved-pod emission >= 2,000 tokens/sec, subject to the configuration in Appendix A (pre-warm schedule, model variant, quantization profile).
2) Measurement & exceptions: Measurements are taken at Redwood's edge; customer telemetry probes will be used to corroborate end-to-end performance. Any divergence will trigger a joint review within 24 hours.
3) Credits: For p99 TTFT violations exceeding 1% of requests in a 24-hour window, Redwood will apply a credit equal to 10% of the POC day's invoice. Repeated violations (3+ days within a 30-day window) allow ClearSky to request a remediation plan and pause traffic routing until completed.
4) Fallback policy: Redwood will implement an automatic fallback to a smaller model variant when sustained queuing is detected; the fallback will be documented and can be disabled by mutual agreement for the POC.

Action items: 1) Elena, confirm you and TechOps can run the synthetic probe we propose (simple 8-token prompt every 30s) in your staging environment. 2) Aditya / Vanessa, include the Appendix A draft and proposed pricing tiers and we can convert to DocuSign.

Regards,
Lauren Bishop
Director, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
